items_missed: No 'How are you today?' — went straight from greeting to intake, even though the customer opened by saying his movers had bailed on him hours earlier.

Agenda statement was incomplete: 'in order for us to walk you through how our pricing works and give you the full estimate I need to ask you some questions... would that be okay' had the roadmap and the confirmation but no 10-15 minute timeframe, so the agenda-opener flag does not hit.

Never asked the stressor question ('Is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?') — the customer handed her the answer unprompted ('I'm desperate', 'I need to be out of here by the end of the month') and she never named it back.
Never probed storage stops or additional stops.

Missed the mobility equipment entirely as a probe item: the customer said there are 'three wheelchairs here, a mobility scooter, and two power chairs' plus a wheelchair too wide for the bedroom closet door. None of that was captured, confirmed, or reflected in the estimate.

No Worries Damage Coverage was started and then abandoned — 'we have no worry damage coverage included on the early weight' was cut off by the customer and she never circled back. The $2,000 figure and what it covers were never said, and the 60c/lb baseline never came up.
No full 'no hidden fees' pitch — she said everything is included, but never the explicit no-credit-card-fee / no-transportation-fee / no-fuel-surcharge / no-assembly-fee list.

Clock section almost entirely missing: the 2.5 hour minimum was stated, but not that the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, not the 15-minute prorated increments after the minimum, and no sense-check.

Estimate variables were collected but never explained as time drivers — the second-floor elevator and the two walk distances were asked about and then never tied to the 3.5 hour estimate. No equivalents (school bus reference) used.

No Save Your Ass prep speech: no consolidation examples (loose items in drawers, photos off walls, kids' toys), no 'take a carload' tip, no 'does that make sense' close. Only a passing 'that would really depend on how well prepared you are when we get there.'
Never explained the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email.
Never gave office hours or how to reach us beyond 'give us a call at any time' for cancellations.
Never used the customer's name once after spending nearly a minute collecting it.
top_strength: Budget-conscious framing on a customer who was clearly panicking about money and time. After quoting 3.5 hours at $742, she immediately volunteered the floor — 'in case if you just end up the minimum, our minimum is only $550. That would really depend on how well prepared you are when we get there' — which gave a desperate customer a lower number to hold onto and an incentive to prep. She also handled a very rambling, repetitive caller with real patience and closed the booking cleanly, including a clear no-deposit reassurance: 'There's no deposit required, no risk in securing your spot.'
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: you left three differentiators and the whole Save Your Ass speech on the table on a call the customer had already decided to buy on — that is free score and free margin. When the customer interrupted your No Worries line, come back to it: 'Real quick, I want to make sure you have this — No Worries Damage Coverage is included, up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse accidental damage. And a few days before, we'll email you your mover's photo and info so you know exactly who's showing up. And if we miss your arrival window, we start discounting immediately.' Then run the prep speech, because on this move it was worth real dollars to him: 'Eugene, anything you can consolidate before we get there makes the move shorter and your bill smaller — loose items out of drawers into boxes, photos off the walls, and anything small you can take a carload of yourself. Does that make sense?' Second priority: use his name. You spent 45 seconds getting 'Eugene Bridges' and then never said it again — on a caller who told you he'd been let down that same day, his name plus one line back to his actual worry ('I know you're on a deadline to be out — we'll get you handled tomorrow afternoon') costs nothing and is the difference between polite and reassuring. Third: finish the clock explanation. You gave the 2.5 hour minimum but not that the clock starts on-site when the contract opens or that it bills in 15-minute increments after that — with a customer this focused on price, that gap is a post-move dispute waiting to happen.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and genuinely patient with a difficult caller, and 'No problem, we'll go ahead and help you get through this' was a real response to his distress, but the call is dominated by long strings of 'Mm-hmm' filler, the customer's name is never used, and his two biggest emotional facts (abandoned by movers that day, wheelchair user) go unacknowledged.
audio_review_reason: Cannot judge clarity or pace from this transcript — the rep's own greeting comes through garbled twice ('Hello good afternoon his moving this is a how can I help') and several of her lines are fragmentary, so it is unclear whether she is hard to understand on the phone or the ASR simply struggled. Worth a listen given she scored low on the clarity/pace bonus bullet.
